audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff is EVEN, full.diffRating 5.5/10, full.carryRating 6/10, and full.tldr reads 'Free stacking lane - every Q volley builds your execute while he farms politely.' The tldr is boilerplate: that exact string appears 26 times across mel.full.js. audit.why: A 550-range mage with one root, no dash and no self-peel against a tank with three dashes, a pull, a stun and a 250-range ult is not an even lane. Every other signal in the file already says K'Sante is ahead; only the difficulty label and the tldr disagree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Ntofo Strikes (Q) a knockup in six places: 'his Q knockup', 'his Q projectile knockup', 'Q knockup + W dash'. Ntofo Strikes does not knock up. Riot's text: 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' The Q kit flags are projectile / hardCC / slow, with no knockup. K'Sante's only knockups are Path Maker (W) and All Out (R). The entry also frames Path Maker as a 'W block' that 'negates your poke'; it is a charge-up that takes reduced damage and then dashes with a knockback and stun, so it soaks damage rather than blocking projectiles.
audit.why: Pull versus knockup changes where Mel stands. A pull drags her toward him, which makes max-range spacing the counterplay and makes standing just outside 450 a trap rather than safety. Calling it a knockup teaches the reader the CC is unavoidable once in the area, which is the wrong lesson for an immobile mage.
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes is a two-stack pull; Path Maker is the charge that soaks the volley and stuns on release.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry mentions that All Out removes Path Maker's own CC. Riot's W text: 'When All Out, deals increased damage and no longer knocks back or stuns.'
audit.why: This is the most decision-changing fact in the matchup for an immobile mage. Once K'Sante ults, his follow-up W is damage only and cannot re-CC Mel. So the R knockback is the single beat she has to survive; after it she is running from a dash that cannot lock her down, not eating a chain. Not knowing this is what makes players hold Flash one beat too long.
audit.corrected: Stated in report[5] Key Ability Interactions and in the loading line.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (W: 'When All Out, deals increased damage and no longer knocks back or stuns')

audit.whatIsWrong: Path Maker deals true damage (kit flag trueDamage on W) and the entry never says so. _missing-interactions.json flags the same thing as 'resistances-invalidated'.
audit.why: The instinct against a tank top laner is to buy MR or HP. Against the one ability that opens his all-in, resistances do nothing. That changes the level 4-5 advice from 'survive at higher HP' to 'do not be inside 600 units at all'.
audit.corrected: Folded into phases[3].why, which is the Levels 4-5 slot.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers at all. Worse, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dontsFull[2].d and report[3].t all claim Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'. Rebuttal's cooldown is 38/35/33/29/26.
audit.why: Twenty seconds is wrong by nearly double at rank 1, and it is exactly the number a reader uses to decide whether to spend the barrier on chip. Under-reporting it makes Rebuttal look cheap. Meanwhile Ntofo Strikes is up every 3.5s flat, so 'wait out his Q' is not a plan - the punishable cooldowns are Path Maker at 14s and Footwork at 10s.
audit.corrected: All Out 120/100/80, Path Maker 14s rank 1, Footwork 10s rank 1, Ntofo Strikes 3.5s flat, Rebuttal 38s rank 1. Fixed in breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.trading; tradeBad and dontsFull[2].d carry the identical string 4x in the file so the applier cannot target them - see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[11] Common Mistakes lists 'Force full rotations into full-HP tank stats' and two generic lines. It never names the mistake this matchup actually produces.
audit.why: The real error is spending the Q rotation into a Path Maker charge, which is precisely when the damage is reduced, and misspacing against Ntofo Strikes because the entry told the reader it lifts. Both are matchup-specific and both are correctable.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the two mistakes the kit actually punishes.

audit.why: The four content spikes (Lvl 2 root window, Lvl 6 All Out, first-item gap-close, late scaling) are the right beats. Only the first-item spike needed the Q wording repaired.

edits.before: Open careful and cash the one clean window you get: at 2, Solar Snare's root into a full Q barrage is a guaranteed punish when he steps up — and even that is only a coin-flip, because his W block and Q knockup answer straight back. From 3 the lane slides his way: he blocks your Q with W, walks you down off one root, and you have no dash to reset the trade. Stack Overwhelm off safe pokes, hold Rebuttal to eat his Q knockup, and treat every trade past level 3 as something to escape from cleanly rather than something to win.

notes: I read tools/apply-proposals.js to get its real rules rather than guess, and two structural blockers fall out of it - both need a manual pass because no proposal can express them. (1) Full-layer short fields are unreachable: line 177 refuses any full-layer edit whose `before` is under 12 characters. That covers diff ('EVEN'), tone, diffRating ('5.5/10'), carryRating and every phases[N].side. So the wrong EVEN / 5.5/10 label and the phases chart cannot be fixed by proposal. This matchup should read HARD / #ff5d6c / 7.5/10 / carry 8/10, and phases[2..5].side should read K'Sante to match content.win. Note the length rule is NOT the obstacle - line 80 skips the drift check entirely when `before` is under 25 chars. (2) Boilerplate defeats the exact-match requirement: line 186 refuses a `before` that occurs more than once in the file. full.tldr here is byte-identical across 26 entries in mel.full.js, and the 'gone for twenty seconds' sentence occurs 4x inside this one entry (tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dontsFull[2].d, report[3].t). I could only repair the copy inside breakdown.trading; the other three still carry the wrong number. FACTUAL: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26, never twenty seconds - worth a global find-and-replace across mel.full.js, since the same sentence is templated into other matchups too. Minor applier bug, unrelated to this matchup: at line 206 the else-branch references an undeclared `chunk`, but it is unreachable because full-layer edits already `continue` at line 189 and checkEdit rejects any other layer, so it never fires.
